title: God Gathers His Scattered People
overview: The LORD promises to replace failed leaders, strengthen his people, and bring the scattered tribes of Israel home from distant lands.

parts.label: Rain from the LORD (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The spring rain ripened the grain before the long dry summer, so people are told to ask the LORD for it, not household idols or fortune-tellers whose promises came to nothing. Trusting those false guides left the people lost and hurt, like sheep with no one to look after them.

parts.label: Bad leaders, new strength (v. 3)
parts.note: The shepherds and the male goats that lead a flock stand for Israel's rulers, who had failed the people. God says he will deal with them and care for his flock himself, turning timid sheep into something like a proud war horse.

parts.label: Leaders from Judah itself (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: The cornerstone holds a building together, and the tent peg holds up a tent and everything hung on it, so these images point to steady leadership coming from Judah rather than from foreign rulers. Christians later read the cornerstone as pointing to Jesus.

parts.label: Both kingdoms restored (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: Joseph and Ephraim mean the northern tribes, carried off by Assyria long before, while Judah was the southern kingdom. God promises to bring both back with such compassion that it will be as if he had never rejected them.

parts.label: Called home from far away (vv. 8-10)
parts.note: God will whistle for his people the way a herder calls animals, and they will return from Egypt and Assyria, the south and north ends of their known world. Gilead in the east and Lebanon in the north mark the edges of the land, which will be too crowded to hold them all.

parts.label: A path through the sea (vv. 11-12)
parts.note: The drying sea and Nile echo the old story of God leading Israel out of Egypt through the sea. The proud powers that once oppressed them will fall, and the people will live safely under God's name.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this promise was fulfilled in Israel's history after the exile, is fulfilled spiritually in the church, or still points to a future literal gathering of the Jewish people.
think: When people you relied on for guidance have let you down, what has helped you decide whom to trust next?
